answer.says: Ramesh, my hunger is no longer a mere abstraction but a concrete demand. Prepare the omelette, toast, and tea. The body, as Jacobi reminds us, cannot be satisfied by the imagination of food alone; it requires the satisfaction of the hunger. Do this quickly, for the spirit requires its material basis.
answer.thought: The hunger is a negation that demands its own resolution. I have rested sufficiently, but the body asserts its right to subsistence, and without it, the contemplation of the dialectic becomes a mere empty form. I must eat to sustain the substance of my thinking.
